disclaimer: Process guidance, not legal advice. Statutory provisions cited for informational purposes; consult qualified counsel for formal proceedings.

rules.title: Organise your evidence
rules.purpose: Consolidate facts, tax invoice, photos, and prior communications into a single verifiable case record.
rules.action: Collect tax invoice, unboxing or damage photos/video, payment transaction ID, and timestamped screenshots of customer service interactions.
rules.caveat: Preserve original electronic files and email headers. Unsubstantiated claims are routinely rejected during grievance review.

rules.title: Escalate to Platform Grievance Officer
rules.purpose: Issue a formal written notice to the designated Grievance Officer under Indian e-commerce regulations.
rules.action: Send a formal factual complaint citing order details, statutory acknowledgement timeframe, and desired relief.
rules.caveat: Under Rule 5(4) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, the Grievance Officer must acknowledge receipt within 48 hours and redress the complaint within one month (Rule 5(5)).

rules.title: Lodge grievance on National Consumer Helpline (NCH / INGRAM)
rules.purpose: Engage the Government of India's pre-litigation conciliation platform to mediate with the company.
rules.action: Register the grievance via consumerhelpline.gov.in, call 1915, or WhatsApp 8800001915 with company details and invoice.
rules.caveat: NCH is an alternate dispute resolution and conciliation mechanism, not a judicial court. Many e-commerce platforms are convergence partners; resolution target is typically 45–60 days.

rules.title: File Consumer Commission petition via e-Jagriti
rules.purpose: Seek binding judicial adjudication and compensation from the District Consumer Commission if mediation fails.
rules.action: Prepare petition, affidavit, and index of documents on the official e-Jagriti portal (e-jagriti.gov.in) for District Commission hearing.
rules.caveat: Statutory limitation period is 2 years from the date cause of action arose (Section 69, Consumer Protection Act, 2019). While self-representation is permitted, consider seeking independent legal advice.
